title: Bank 5-day work week: UFBU-IBA meeting fails to resolve issue; check strike dates, other details- Moneycontrol.com

Check what happens next and the key dates   September 04, 2026 / 17:01 IST             The five-day banking week dispute has intensified after the United Forum of Bank Unions ( UFBU ), an umbrella body representing major  bank  employee and officer unions, held a meeting with the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) on September 4, but failed to reach a positive outcome. Following the meeting, the UFBU said it was not in a position to defer its planned nationwide bank strike on September 11, 2026. “The meeting between UFBU and IBA held today ended without any positive outcome on our key demands. With the issues of 5-Day Banking, discriminatory PLI, and other pending/residual issues remaining unresolved, there is no reason to defer the strike call,” UFBU said on X post. The UFBU represents seven bank employee and officer unions -- All India Bank Employees Association, All India Bank Officers' Confederation, National Confederation of Bank Employees, All India Bank Officers' Association, Bank Employees Federation of India, Indian National Bank Employees Federation, and INBOC. What happened at the UFBU-IBA meeting? According to the UFBU's latest communication, the IBA had invited representatives of the bank unions for discussions on the issues raised in the strike notice. The IBA reportedly appealed to the unions to defer the proposed strike and continue discussions through bilateral negotiations. However, the UFBU maintained that the issues have remained unresolved for too long and that there was no concrete development that would justify postponing the agitation. Why are bank unions demanding five-day banking? The five-day banking demand is linked to the agreement reached between the IBA and bank unions under the March 8, 2024 settlement and joint note. Under the proposal, Saturdays other than the second and fourth Saturdays would become holidays, while employees would work additional hours from Monday to Friday. The arrangement envisages an increase of around 40 minutes in daily working hours from Monday to Friday so that customer-facing business hours are not reduced. The unions have argued that the proposal was subsequently recommended to the government but has remained pending for more than two years. The UFBU has therefore been pressing the government to approve and implement the five-day banking arrangement. What is the dispute over the PLI scheme? The unions are also opposing the government's revised PLI scheme for senior bank officers. UFBU says the earlier understanding with the IBA was that PLI would be linked to the overall performance of the bank and that the number of incentive days would be uniform for employees and officers up to Scale VII. The government, however, has directed banks to implement a different structure for Scale IV officers and above. Under this framework, senior officers could receive PLI of up to 365 days of basic pay plus dearness allowance, while officers up to Scale III would have a maximum of 15 days, according to the UFBU circular. The unions have termed the structure discriminatory and want its implementation kept in abeyance until the scheme is discussed bilaterally with unions. Bank strike dates: What happens next? With the September 4 meeting failing to produce a settlement, the current UFBU strike programme remains: September 11, 2026: One-day nationwide bank strike September 28-30, 2026: Three-day nationwide bank strike From October 26, 2026: Indefinite nationwide strike The September 11 strike is therefore expected to proceed unless there is a fresh breakthrough between the unions, IBA and the government. For bank customers, a strike could affect branch operations and some banking services on the affected dates. Digital banking channels such as internet banking, mobile banking and ATMs may continue to operate, although the availability of individual services can vary by bank. UFBU-IBA talks fail to break the deadlock, with unions deciding to proceed with the September 11 strike. Check what happens next and the key dates

September 04, 2026 / 17:01 IST

The five-day banking week dispute has intensified after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), an umbrella body representing major bank employee and officer unions, held a meeting with the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) on September 4, but failed to reach a positive outcome. Following the meeting, the UFBU said it was not in a position to defer its planned nationwide bank strike on September 11, 2026.

“The meeting between UFBU and IBA held today ended without any positive outcome on our key demands. With the issues of 5-Day Banking, discriminatory PLI, and other pending/residual issues remaining unresolved, there is no reason to defer the strike call,” UFBU said on X post.

The UFBU represents seven bank employee and officer unions -- All India Bank Employees Association, All India Bank Officers' Confederation, National Confederation of Bank Employees, All India Bank Officers' Association, Bank Employees Federation of India, Indian National Bank Employees Federation, and INBOC.

What happened at the UFBU-IBA meeting?

According to the UFBU's latest communication, the IBA had invited representatives of the bank unions for discussions on the issues raised in the strike notice. The IBA reportedly appealed to the unions to defer the proposed strike and continue discussions through bilateral negotiations. However, the UFBU maintained that the issues have remained unresolved for too long and that there was no concrete development that would justify postponing the agitation.

Why are bank unions demanding five-day banking?

The five-day banking demand is linked to the agreement reached between the IBA and bank unions under the March 8, 2024 settlement and joint note. Under the proposal, Saturdays other than the second and fourth Saturdays would become holidays, while employees would work additional hours from Monday to Friday.

The arrangement envisages an increase of around 40 minutes in daily working hours from Monday to Friday so that customer-facing business hours are not reduced. The unions have argued that the proposal was subsequently recommended to the government but has remained pending for more than two years.

The UFBU has therefore been pressing the government to approve and implement the five-day banking arrangement.

What is the dispute over the PLI scheme?

The unions are also opposing the government's revised PLI scheme for senior bank officers. UFBU says the earlier understanding with the IBA was that PLI would be linked to the overall performance of the bank and that the number of incentive days would be uniform for employees and officers up to Scale VII.

The government, however, has directed banks to implement a different structure for Scale IV officers and above. Under this framework, senior officers could receive PLI of up to 365 days of basic pay plus dearness allowance, while officers up to Scale III would have a maximum of 15 days, according to the UFBU circular. The unions have termed the structure discriminatory and want its implementation kept in abeyance until the scheme is discussed bilaterally with unions.

Bank strike dates: What happens next?

With the September 4 meeting failing to produce a settlement, the current UFBU strike programme remains:

September 11, 2026: One-day nationwide bank strike

September 28-30, 2026: Three-day nationwide bank strike

From October 26, 2026: Indefinite nationwide strike

The September 11 strike is therefore expected to proceed unless there is a fresh breakthrough between the unions, IBA and the government.

For bank customers, a strike could affect branch operations and some banking services on the affected dates. Digital banking channels such as internet banking, mobile banking and ATMs may continue to operate, although the availability of individual services can vary by bank.
